h1: Hot water or steam from cylinder discharge
title: Hot water or steam from cylinder discharge | G3 Cylinder Help
description: Understand hot water or steam from cylinder discharge. Distinguish the symptom, gather useful details and arrange competent cylinder assessment in London.
answer: Very hot water or steam from a safety discharge requires urgent attention. Keep clear and do not touch, obstruct or adjust the discharge.

sections.heading: What this symptom can mean
paragraphs: For temperature-and-pressure relief discharge on the Megaflo Eco described in its manual, stop the heat source or immersion using ordinary controls if safe and contact a competent unvented engineer. The manufacturer says not to turn off the water supply for that condition.

sections.heading: Information to gather safely
paragraphs: Do not remove covers, reset a concealed cut-out, cap pipework or attempt to make a valve stop by force. Follow the correct appliance user safety instructions; other product types can have different instructions.

sections.heading: How the enquiry becomes an investigation
paragraphs: The cylinder make, full model and heating arrangement should be identified first. The same visible symptom can arise from different causes, and a relief device may be protecting the system rather than creating the original problem. Component testing and any repair belong to a person competent for the work.

sections.heading: Discuss the appropriate next step
paragraphs: Call 020 7205 4433 with the postcode, symptom history and any previous service findings. The enquiry establishes the proposed assessment and availability. Do not use this guide as a substitute for the actual appliance safety instructions or an on-site diagnosis.

faqs.question: Should I shut the Megaflo water supply for temperature-and-pressure relief discharge?
faqs.answer: The Megaflo Eco manual says to stop the heat source and leave the water supply on; seek urgent competent assessment.
